newsitem.title: USA: Coca-Cola shrs off, Morgan sees growth.
newsitem.headline: Coca-Cola shrs off, Morgan sees growth.

text.p: Coca-Cola Co is likely to post growth of about seven percent in gallon and volume shipments in the fourth quarter, Morgan Stanley analyst Andrew Conway said.
The company reported third quarter earnings of $0.39 versus $0.32 a year ago. The company said the quarter results included an after-tax charge of $200 million to reduce concentrate inventory levels.
Conway described the charge as a "prudent action...which puts them on track to grow earnings per share by 17 percent in 1996."
Conway maintained his 1996 estimate at $1.38 per share, and the 1997 estimate of $1.64.
He said his 12-month price target was $55. Shares fell 3/4 to 48-1/4.
Coca-Cola said third quarter worldwide unit case volume rose six percent, and grew five percent in the U.S.
